title: Curaçao Jewish Heritage Journey
subtitle: Join Rabbi Joel Sisenwine and TBE congregant and Curaçao native Susan Alvares Correa as we embark on a remarkable journey to Curaçao, a Caribbean island with an extraordinary Jewish heritage, vibrant culture, and breathtaking beauty.
about_company: L’Dor Vador Travel brings to life the compelling stories of Jewish migration across the Atlantic. Its founders combine backgrounds in journalism and bespoke travel with three decades of experience in special-interest tourism in destinations such as Cuba and Suriname. Guided by curiosity and a commitment to historical depth, LDVD looks beyond the familiar to create meaningful connections between travelers and the people, places, and stories that shape a destination. A hands-on, service-minded approach ensures a seamless journey, allowing travelers to engage fully with one of Jewish history’s most remarkable, seldom-told chapters: how Jewish life crossed the Atlantic, found hope, took root, and flourished in Curaçao.

intro:
Join Rabbi Joel Sisenwine and TBE congregant and Curaçao native Susan Alvares Correa as we embark on a remarkable journey to Curaçao, a Caribbean island with an extraordinary Jewish heritage, vibrant culture, and breathtaking beauty.

Together, we’ll meet members of today’s Jewish community, explore the people and places that shaped this enduring legacy, share Shabbat and Havdalah, and taste the flavors and traditions that have been passed down through generations. We’ll also venture into Bandabou, rural Curaçao, to encounter Curaçao’s Afro-Curaçaoan history, art, and music, placing the island’s Jewish story within the broader cultural and historical landscape in which it developed.

From the historic Mikvé Israel-Emanuel Synagogue (home to the oldest continuously active Jewish congregation in the Americas), to centuries-old Jewish cemeteries, historic family homes, and the colorful streets of Willemstad, we’ll trace more than 375 years of Jewish life and reflect on a unique Jewish legacy that continues to thrive.

itinerary.title: The Sephardic Story of Curaçao
itinerary.subtitle: Day Program: 9:00 AM–4:00 PM | Group Dinner at Caleo
itinerary.text:
Breakfast
- Enjoy the breakfast buffet at our resort.

Historic Willemstad
- We begin with a drive through Willemstad, a UNESCO World Heritage city renowned for its distinctive and colorful colonial architecture.

Mikvé Israel-Emanuel Synagogue — The Snoa
- Continue to Mikvé Israel-Emanuel Synagogue, affectionately known as the Snoa.
- Completed in 1732, it is the oldest continuously operating synagogue in the Americas and connects us to a Sephardic Jewish story whose Spanish and Portuguese roots can be traced to the Iberian Peninsula of the 1400s.
- Here, we meet the spiritual leader of the Snoa, Rabbi Martin Hirsch, who is originally from Chile. 
- While at the Snoa, we have the opportunity to learn firsthand from one of the world's leading scholars on the history of Jews in Curaçao, Ron Gomes Casseres. Ron has written extensively on the topic, and can trace his personal family's history back to Sephardic immigrants who arrived on the island in 1690. Aside from his dozens of publications, he has been decorated by the Kingdom of the Netherlands for social and cultural contributions to the Curaçao community.

Jewish Museum Curaçao
- Explore the newly expanded and renovated Jewish Museum at your own pace with an audio tour, or choose to join a highlights tour with museum curator, Phyllis Meit. Phyllis is a wealth of knowledge, and is happy to share her family's unique history of how they arrived to the island via Romania.

Lunch at La Vie en Rose
- Delight in a high-tea-style lunch at La Vie en Rose, in the historic district of Scharloo, known for its elegant colonial mansions, many of which were once owned by prosperous Jewish merchants during the 19th century.

Curaçao's Historic Jewish Cemeteries
- On our way back to the hotel, we will pass the newer Jewish cemetery established in 1864, as well as historic Beth Haim Blenheim Cemetery.
- Established in 1659 by Curaçao's first 12 Jewish families, Beth Haim Blenheim is the oldest Jewish cemetery in the Caribbean. Its richly carved tombstones preserve the story of Curaçao's early Sephardic community and its far-reaching Atlantic connections.

Evening in Kura Hulanda
- Step into a walkable village within the city, Kura Hulanda - a beautifully restored area of the inner city that boasts dimly lit restaurants, live music, inviting public plazas, galleries, as well as our restaurant for the evening, Caleo.

Punda Vibes
- On Thursday nights, Punda's streets fill with local vendors, live music, open bars, and fireworks! Fireworks take place at 8:15pm, and are visible from many places in Punda or Otrobanda, including just outside our restaurant.
itinerary.overnight: Renaissance Wind Creek Curaçao Resort, Willemstad

itinerary.title: Jewish Legacies in Art, Architecture & Culture
itinerary.subtitle: Day Program: 9:00 AM–4:00 PM | Kabbalat Shabbat Under the Stars
itinerary.text:
Breakfast
- Enjoy the breakfast buffet at our resort.

Mongui Maduro Historic House
- Visit this meticulously preserved historic plantation house and discover the legacy of the Levy Maduro family, a prominent Sephardic Jewish lineage that significantly influenced Curaçao's economic and social landscape over four generations.

Landhuis Bloemhof & Cathedral of Thorns
- Continue to Landhuis Bloemhof, which today houses a cultural center dedicated to art, heritage, and nature.
- Learn about the history and ideals of the family that has continued to innovate at Bloemhof across generations.
- Visit the extraordinary Cathedral of Thorns, conceived as a space for reflection and healing and as a powerful metaphor for Curaçao's complex history, including colonialism and slavery.

Lunch at Number Ten
- Enjoy lunch together at Number Ten.

Chobolobo Distillery
- Discover the history and production of Curaçao's iconic Blue Curaçao liqueur, invented by a local Sephardic Jewish family.

Kabbalat Shabbat
- As the sun begins to set, we come together for Kabbalat Shabbat at the Snoa.

Shabbat Dinner
- Following services, return to the resort for an outdoor Shabbat dinner, celebrating the arrival of Shabbat together in Curaçao.
itinerary.overnight: Renaissance Wind Creek Curaçao Resort, Willemstad

itinerary.title: Curaçaoan Jewry in Practice and on Paper
itinerary.subtitle: Shabbat Morning Service: 9:30 AM - 12:00 PM  | Havdalah & Dinner in Otrobanda
itinerary.text:
Breakfast
- Enjoy the breakfast buffet at our resort.

Shabbat Morning Services at the Snoa
- This Shabbat morning service, unique to the island, features prayers in Papiamentu, Portuguese, Dutch, Hebrew, English and Spanish. The service, mainly in English and Hebrew, takes place in the sanctuary almost three centuries old, complete with a rare sand floor, and stunning mahogany woodwork throughout.

Time for reflection and exploration
- After Shabbat morning services, the afternoon is intentionally left free of scheduled programming, allowing everyone to experience the island at their own pace.
- During this time, return to the hotel's infinity pool, or take a self-guided exploratory walk through Willemstad's historic center.
- A variety of optional excursions and activities will be offered by your hosts.

Havdalah on the Beach
- Join our group at the resort's poolside "beach" for a breezy embrace of the senses as we celebrate Havdalah, before strolling over to a local art gallery for bites, books, art, and literature.

Art, Books & Dinner in Historic Otrobanda
- Walk over with the group to Sebastopol 9, an art gallery housed in a monumental 18th-century residence that has remained in the same family for roughly three centuries. Today, Philip Chapman and his brothers have given the property a new cultural life as a gallery showcasing emerging Curaçaoan artists.
- Enjoy a private catered dinner buffet inside the gallery, surrounded by contemporary local art.
- During the evening, meet Anneroos Reich, a bookstore owner, active member of Curaçao's Jewish community, and board member of the Jewish Museum. Especially for our group, she will open her bookstore Hirsch & Reich outside of opening hours, presenting a curated selection of books relevant to our journey, including Judaica, regional history, literature, art, and culture.
- This encounter also offers an informal opportunity to speak with Anneroos about contemporary Jewish life in Curaçao and everyday island life, connecting the historical Jewish story explored throughout our journey with the community that lives it today.

After Dinner — Evening at Leisure
- Stroll back to the hotel at your own pace, or continue exploring the historic Otrobanda neighborhood by night. Your hotel is an easy 5-minute stroll away.
itinerary.overnight: Renaissance Wind Creek Curaçao Resort, Willemstad

itinerary.title: Afro-Curaçaoan Identity, History, and Art
itinerary.subtitle: Day Program: 9:00 AM - 4:00 PM | Farewell Dinner
itinerary.text:
Breakfast
- Enjoy the breakfast buffet at our resort.

Depart for Bandabou
- Travel west into Bandabou, Curaçao's rural western region, where plantation history, Afro-Curaçaoan traditions, and the island's struggle for freedom remain deeply embedded in the landscape.

Tula Museum at Landhuis Kenepa
- Visit the Tula Museum, housed at the former Kenepa plantation, one of the principal sites associated with Curaçao's great slave revolt of 1795.
- We are personally welcomed by Jeanne Henriquez, historian, activist, and director of the museum.
- Through the story of Tula, leader of the 1795 uprising and today recognized as a national hero of Curaçao, Jeanne introduces us to the history of slavery, resistance, emancipation, and the continuing process of confronting Curaçao's colonial past.
- Our conversation moves beyond history to explore nation-building, national identity, collective memory, and the importance of national heroes.

Santa Cruz
- Continue to Santa Cruz, a secluded beach nestled within one of Bandabou's beautiful natural coves.
- We are joined by Pernell Saturnino, Grammy Award-winning percussionist and Berklee College of Music alumnus, for an encounter with Curaçao's musical heritage.
- Pernell introduces us to traditional Afro-Curaçaoan rhythms and instruments, including the chapi and tambú, and explores how rhythm, music, resistance, spirituality, and community are intertwined in Curaçaoan culture.
- Enjoy a breezy, open-air buffet-style lunch at the legendary home base of Juni "Captain Goodlife" Obersi, one of the island's colorful local personalities. Refresh with a cocktail on the shaded terrace overlooking the bay, or enjoy a leisurely stroll along the beach. This lunch interlude offers an opportunity to experience another side of life in rural Curaçao before continuing our journey.

Art, Rhythm & Curaçaoan Identity: Yubi Kirindongo & Pernell Saturnino
- Continue to the home and atelier of internationally renowned Curaçaoan artist Yubi Kirindongo.
- Known especially for transforming discarded materials into powerful works of art, Kirindongo has developed a distinctive visual language rooted in Curaçao, the African diaspora, social consciousness, and the transformation of what society has cast aside. He personally welcomes us into his world and introduces us to his life, artistic philosophy, and work.
- Drinks/Cocktails will be provided.

Farewell Dinner
- On our final night in Curaçao, we unite for a festive open-air farewell dinner at our resort.
- Over dinner, we reflect on the people we have met, the stories we have encountered, and all that we have experienced together during our Caribbean journey.
